sa.q: Differentiate between an Association of Persons (AOP) and a Body of Individuals (BOI).
sa.a: A BOI consists only of individuals who join together to earn income collectively, whereas an AOP can have any person (individuals, companies, firms) as members joining for a common purpose or action.

sa.q: Explain the concept of 'Diversion of income by overriding title'.
sa.a: It signifies the diversion of income at source before it reaches the assessee due to a legal compulsion or contractual obligation. Such income is excluded from the assessee's assessable income because it never legally becomes their income.

sa.q: Under what circumstances is the income of an assessee taxed in the same tax year rather than the subsequent year?
sa.a: Exceptions include: shipping business of non-residents, persons leaving India without intention to return, an AOP/BOI formed for a particular event likely to be dissolved, persons transferring property to avoid tax, and discontinued businesses.

sa.q: What is Marginal Relief and when is it applicable?
sa.a: Marginal Relief ensures that the increase in income tax (due to surcharge) does not exceed the actual increase in total income when it crosses specified thresholds (like ₹50 lakhs, ₹1 crore). It is applicable to all categories of assessees facing a sudden tax spike due to surcharge brackets.

essay.q: Examine the tests applied to distinguish between a Capital Receipt and a Revenue Receipt. Provide relevant examples.
essay.a: Distinguishing capital and revenue receipts is crucial because only revenue receipts are normally taxable unless specified otherwise (like capital gains). Tests include: 1. Fixed vs Circulating Capital: Receipts from fixed capital (e.g., sale of a building by a manufacturer) are capital, while from circulating capital (stock-in-trade) are revenue. 2. Transaction in course of business: Sale of shares by a broker is revenue, by an investor is capital. 3. Compensation for termination of agency: If the agency is the sole business, it's a capital receipt; if it's one of many, it's revenue. Ultimately, the nature depends on the facts and circumstances of each case.

essay.q: Explain the significance of the various components of Income-tax Law in India.
essay.a: The Income-tax Law comprises: 1. Income-tax Act: The primary statute governing definitions, charging, deductions, and administration. 2. Annual Finance Act: Passed annually to amend the IT Act and specify current tax rates. 3. Income-tax Rules: Detailed procedures prescribed by the CBDT for executing the Act. 4. Circulars & Notifications: Issued by CBDT for clarification, binding on the department to ensure uniform application, but not on assessees. 5. Judicial Decisions: Rulings by the Supreme Court (law of the land) and High Courts that interpret ambiguous provisions and settle disputes between the department and taxpayers.
